posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
Not really many non-script solutions, no. Neither VX or VXAce have native mouse support, so if you have your heart set on a point-and-click but aren't confident in using scripts, VX may not the easiest engine for your project.
You could look for a keyboard workaround like EntangledPear suggested--one of the "picture menu" or "evented menu" tutorials in the tutorials section might be able to help you with that.
Alternatively, MV and MZ have mouse support right out of the box, so perhaps look at getting one of those next time they go on sale?

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Back to the original question:
not without a lot of scripts - VX doesn't even have native mouse support, much less anything like "click on button/picture" functionality.
You CAN change the engine with scripts enough to enable all those functions, but as said it requires a lot of scripts - of which I don't know if they ever existed, much less if they still exist now.
At one time, VXA had all scripts required for that - but despite best efforts a lot of scripts were lost in the two decades since then. And VX is another five years older and the community wasn't as organised then as it became beginning with VXA.
Is there a specific reason why you want to use VX? If you search for steam sales you can get either VXA or MV for less than 10$ several times a year.
